blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: form the passive with ser + participle and know when it is used
describe a result with estar + participle
use se for passive and impersonal statements (se habla español, se dice que)
talk about accidents with se me ... (se me olvidó, se me cayó)

blocks.text: In an active sentence the subject does the action (Cervantes escribió el libro). In a passive sentence the object becomes the subject: ser (in any tense) + past participle, which agrees with the new subject. The doer is introduced by por.

head: Tense
Example
English
rows: La casa es limpiada cada semana.
The house is cleaned every week.
El libro fue escrito por Cervantes.
The book was written by Cervantes.
Las cartas eran enviadas por correo.
The letters were sent by post.
The door will be opened tomorrow.

items: Agreement: la casa fue construida, los edificios fueron construidos, las casas fueron construidas.
The passive with ser is common in written Spanish (news, history, formal texts) and rare in speech. In speech Spanish uses the active voice or se (section 3).
Use it when the doer is mentioned or when the focus is on the receiver: Fue elegida presidenta por los socios.

blocks.title: worden vs ser
blocks.text: Dutch worden (het huis wordt schoongemaakt) and zijn (het huis is schoon) both exist. Spanish uses ser + participle for the action (es limpiada) and estar + participle for the result (está limpia). Dutch werd = fue.

head: Action (ser)
Result (estar)
English
rows: La puerta fue cerrada por el portero.
The door was closed by the porter. / The door is closed.
La cena fue preparada por mi madre.
The dinner was prepared by my mother. / The dinner is ready.
Las ventanas fueron rotas por la tormenta.
The windows were broken by the storm. / The windows are broken.
La carta fue escrita por mi abuelo.
La carta está escrita a mano.
The letter was written by my grandfather. / The letter is handwritten.

blocks.text: Estar + participle also works with adjectives: cansado, abierto, ocupado, preocupado, sentado, enamorado. The participle always agrees: Los museos están cerrados. Ana está sentada.
When the doer does not matter, Spanish prefers se + third person. The verb agrees with the thing (the real subject): singular for one thing, plural for several.

head: Spanish
English
Agreement
rows: Se cerró el museo a las ocho.
The museum was closed at eight.

blocks.title: No agent with se
blocks.text: You cannot add por + person to a se sentence. For a named doer use ser + participle: Fue construido por los romanos, not Se construyó por los romanos.

head: Spanish
English
Pattern
rows: In Spain people have dinner late.
Se dice que va a llover.
They say it is going to rain.
How do you say "hello" in Spanish?

items: Another way to be impersonal is the third person plural: Dicen que va a llover. Llaman a la puerta. Aquí hablan muy rápido. ("they")
Or tú in speech: Si pagas con tarjeta, tienes descuento. ("if you pay ...")
uno is more formal: Uno nunca sabe. (You never know.)

blocks.text: For things that happen to you by accident (not on purpose), Spanish uses se + indirect pronoun + verb. The verb agrees with the thing, and the person becomes the indirect object.

head: Spanish
Literal idea
English
rows: The key forgot itself to me.
The keys forgot themselves to me.
Se te ha roto el móvil.
The passport got lost to him.
The time ran out to us.

blocks.title: Dutch: per ongeluk
blocks.text: Dutch says ik heb het laten vallen (I dropped it); Spanish prefers se me cayó (it fell to me) when it is an accident. The sentence with Rompí el móvil sounds like you did it on purpose, whereas Se me rompió el móvil says it just happened.

rows: The participle agrees with the subject.
The verb agrees with the thing: plural.
Add me and make the verb plural.
The verb agrees with the thing that fell.
se sentences cannot have a por agent.
Se dicen que va a llover.
Se dice que va a llover.

blocks.text: Fill in the missing word or the verb in brackets. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: La catedral ______ construida en el siglo XIII.
items.full: La catedral fue construida en el siglo XIII.

items.q: Ya son las once: la tienda ______ cerrada.
items.full: Ya son las once: la tienda está cerrada.
Se venden pisos en el centro.
Se dice que va a llover.
La novela fue escrita por Cervantes.

items.q: The windows were broken by the storm.
items.a: Las ventanas fueron rotas por la tormenta.
